questions.q: What does the ForEach activity need as its Items input?
options: An array — such as a pipeline variable or a Lookup activity's value output
A single string value
A linked service reference
A boolean expression
questions.explain: ForEach needs a JSON array to iterate over, commonly an array-type pipeline variable or the value array from a Lookup activity with firstRowOnly set to false.

questions.q: How do activities nested inside a ForEach loop reference the current item?
options: @item()
@variables('current')
@pipeline().parameters.item
@trigger().item
questions.explain: @item() returns whatever value the loop is currently on — the first array element on the first pass, the second on the second, and so on.

questions.q: What does setting isSequential to false do?
options: Runs iterations in parallel, up to the batchCount limit, instead of one at a time
Disables the ForEach activity entirely
Forces every iteration to run strictly in array order
Converts the ForEach into an Until activity
questions.explain: isSequential: false (the default) runs iterations in parallel. Setting it to true runs them one at a time, in order — safer when iterations aren't fully independent.

questions.q: Why is running a ForEach in parallel risky when iterations write to the same file or variable?
options: Concurrent iterations racing to write the same target can produce write conflicts or unpredictable results
Parallel ForEach loops can only read data, never write it
It's not actually risky — parallel execution is always safe
Parallel mode automatically serializes writes to prevent conflicts
questions.explain: If concurrent iterations target the exact same file or the exact same pipeline variable, they can genuinely conflict — sequential execution is the safer default unless iterations are truly independent.

questions.q: Can a ForEach activity contain another ForEach activity directly nested inside it?
options: No — nesting isn't supported; use a two-level pipeline with Execute Pipeline instead
Yes, with no limit on nesting depth
Yes, but only up to 2 levels deep
Only if isSequential is set to true on both loops
questions.explain: ForEach can't directly nest another ForEach (or Until). The workaround is an outer ForEach calling an Execute Pipeline activity whose inner pipeline contains the nested loop.
